images.title: One tin can, two profiles
images.purpose: Shows that one solid gives different profiles from different viewpoints: a circle from above and a rectangle from the side.
images.composition: Plain white background with generous empty margins; the main object is large and centred and fills about 60 percent of the frame; nothing else is drawn. A cylinder in the centre; a flat circle above it and a flat rectangle to its right, each joined to the cylinder by one thin grey arrow with its viewpoint name.
images.exact_structure: Centre: an upright cylinder (tin can), outlined dark, body filled teal #0072B2, top ellipse lighter teal. Above it: a flat circle outlined amber #E69F00, radius 3 cm drawn as a thin radius line from the centre dot, labelled 'radius 3 cm'; grey arrow from the circle down to the can's top labelled 'from above'. Right: a flat rectangle outlined green #009E73, width 6 cm, height 10 cm (taller than wide, ratio 3 to 5); grey arrow from the can's side to it labelled 'from the side'; the rectangle's bottom edge labelled '6 cm', its right edge labelled '10 cm'.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The same tin can shows a circle from above and a rectangle from the side.
images.description: Shows that one solid gives different profiles from different viewpoints: a circle from above and a rectangle from the side.
images.context: Concept T5.C2; one image that shows only the main idea.
images.teaching_notes: Rectangle width is the diameter, 2 × 3 = 6 cm.

image_decisions.why: Profiles are a visual idea; one picture with one solid and its two outlines states it directly.
